questions.question:
Which of the following pairs is correct in terms of pH values?

(a) Tooth decay in humans: pH of mouth > 5.5

(b) pH range of human body: 7.0 to 7.8

(c) Acid rain: pH of rain water > 8
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Only (b) is correct.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **pH range of the human body** is approximately **7.0 to 7.8**. This range is essential for maintaining proper biological functions, as the body operates optimally within this slightly alkaline range.
 
• The body's **buffer systems**, such as the bicarbonate buffer system, help maintain this pH range to support **enzyme activity, oxygen transport, and metabolic processes**.
 
• A deviation from this pH range can result in conditions like **acidosis (too acidic)** or **alkalosis (too alkaline)**, which can disrupt essential bodily functions.
 
• This pH range is regulated by organs like the **lungs and kidneys**, which play a crucial role in maintaining acid-base balance in the body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tooth decay in humans: pH of mouth > 5.5**__

 __
 
• This statement is **incorrect** because **tooth decay occurs when the pH of the mouth falls below 5.5**. At this pH level, the enamel, which is primarily composed of hydroxyapatite, begins to demineralize.
 
• Low pH in the mouth is often caused by the presence of **acidic byproducts from bacterial activity** during the breakdown of sugars.
 
• To prevent tooth decay, it is important to maintain good oral hygiene and limit the consumption of sugary foods and drinks.
 
 
 
• **Acid rain: pH of rainwater > 8**__
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect** because **acid rain has a pH less than 5.6**, not greater than 8.
 
• Acid rain is caused by the presence of **sulfur dioxide (SO₂)** and **nitrogen oxides (NOₓ)** in the atmosphere, which react with water to form sulfuric acid and nitric acid.
 
• The impacts of acid rain include damage to **forests, aquatic ecosystems, and buildings**, as well as harm to soil quality.

questions.question: Which of the following solutions has the highest concentration of hydrogen ions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pH = 4**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

 
• **The pH scale is a logarithmic scale** that measures the acidity or basicity of a solution.
 
• It **ranges from 0 to 14,** with 7 being neutral.
 
• A **pH less than 7 indicates an acidic solution**, meaning it has a higher concentration of hydrogen ions (H+). 
 
• A** pH greater than 7 indicates a basic solution**, meaning it has a higher concentration of hydroxide ions (OH-).
 
• The concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution is related to the pH by the following equation
 
 
• pH = -log[H+]
 
 
 
• **Where**:
 
 
• pH is the pH of the solution
 
• [H+] is the concentration of hydrogen ions in moles per liter (M)
 
• From this equation, we can see that a lower pH corresponds to a higher concentration of hydrogen ions.
 
 
 
• A**mong the acidic solutions, pH = 4 is the lowest, **meaning it has the highest concentration of hydrogen ions.
 
• **Therefore, the solution with pH = 4 has the highest concentration of hydrogen ions.**

questions.question: Which of the following is produced when acid reacts with a base?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Salt and water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A reaction between an acid and a base is known as a **neutralization reaction**.
 
• In a neutralization reaction, **salt and water** are formed as products.
 
• This type of reaction typically involves the combination of hydrogen ions (H⁺) from the acid and hydroxide ions (OH⁻) from the base to form water (H₂O).
 
• The general equation for a neutralization reaction is: **Acid + Base → Salt + Water**.
 
• Examples include the reaction between hydrochloric acid (HCl) and sodium hydroxide (NaOH) to produce sodium chloride (NaCl) and water (H₂O).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acids**

 
 
• Acids are substances that release hydrogen ions (H⁺) when dissolved in water.
 
• Common examples include hydrochloric acid (HCl), sulfuric acid (H₂SO₄), and acetic acid (CH₃COOH).
 
 
 
• **Bases**
 
 
• Bases are substances that release hydroxide ions (OH⁻) when dissolved in water.
 
• Common examples include sodium hydroxide (NaOH), potassium hydroxide (KOH), and calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)₂).
 
 
 
• **Salts**
 
 
• Salts are ionic compounds composed of positively charged cations and negatively charged anions.
 
• They are formed as a result of the neutralization reaction between acids and bases.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Neutralization**
 
 
• Neutralization reactions are used in various applications such as antacid formulations, wastewater treatment, and soil pH adjustment.
 
• They help in reducing acidity or alkalinity to maintain a balanced pH level in different environments.

 **Methyl orange**

• Methyl orange shows red** color in acidic medium **and yellow color in basic medium.

questions.question: As the concentration of hydronium ions increases, the pH value _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**decreases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The pH value is a measure of the hydrogen ion concentration in a solution.
 
• As the concentration of hydronium ions (H₃O⁺) increases, the pH value decreases.
 
• A lower pH value indicates a higher acidity of the solution.
 
• The pH scale ranges from 0 to 14, with 7 being neutral, below 7 acidic, and above 7 basic.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Hydronium Ion (H₃O⁺)**

 
 
• Hydronium ion is the form in which a proton (H⁺) exists in aqueous solution.
 
• It is formed when an acid dissolves in water, donating a proton to a water molecule.
 
 
 
• **pH Scale**
 
 
• The pH scale is logarithmic, meaning each whole pH value below 7 is ten times more acidic than the next higher value.
 
• For example, a solution with a pH of 3 is 10 times more acidic than a solution with a pH of 4.
 
 
 
• **Acidity and Alkalinity**
 
 
• Acidity refers to the concentration of hydrogen ions (H⁺) in a solution.
 
• Alkalinity refers to the concentration of hydroxide ions (OH−) in a solution.
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction**
 
 
• A neutralization reaction occurs when an acid and a base react to form water and a salt.
 
• This reaction generally results in the pH of the solution moving towards neutral (pH 7).

questions.question: What is the approximate pH of a neutral salt solution?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Equal to 7**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **neutral salt solution** is formed when a strong acid reacts with a strong base.
 
• The resulting solution has a **pH of 7**, which is considered **neutral**.
 
• **pH** is a scale used to specify the acidity or basicity of an aqueous solution.
 
• A pH of **7** indicates a **neutral** solution, meaning it is neither acidic nor basic.
 
• Examples of neutral salts include **sodium chloride (NaCl)** and **potassium nitrate (KNO₃)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Less than 7**__

 __
 
• A pH less than 7 indicates an **acidic solution**.
 
• This occurs when a **strong acid reacts with a weak base**, producing an acidic salt solution.
 
 
 
• **Depends on the temperature**__
 __
 
• While temperature can slightly affect the pH, a neutral salt solution typically remains close to pH 7.
 
• Extreme temperatures can alter the dissociation of water, but under normal conditions, the effect is minimal.
 
 
 
• **More than 7**__
 
 
• A pH more than 7 indicates a **basic (alkaline) solution**.
 
• This occurs when a **strong base reacts with a weak acid**, producing a basic salt solution.

questions.question: Alkaloids contain ___________.

options.text: Acids which are soluble in water
Acids that are not soluble in water
Bases which are not soluble in water
Bases which are soluble in water

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bases which are soluble in water**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Alkaloids** are naturally occurring organic compounds containing nitrogen, mostly found in plants.
 
• They typically act as **weak bases** due to the presence of an amine group in their structure.
 
• Most alkaloids are **soluble in water**, especially in their salt form (e.g., hydrochloride salts).
 
• These compounds often have pharmacological properties and are widely used in medicine (e.g., morphine, quinine, caffeine).
 
• Alkaloids can form salts with acids, enhancing their solubility in water and increasing their bioavailability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Alkaloids:** Alkaloids are nitrogenous organic compounds derived from plants, fungi, or microorganisms. They are known for their bitter taste and physiological effects on humans and animals.
 
• **Types of Alkaloids:** Examples include purine alkaloids (caffeine), tropane alkaloids (atropine), and isoquinoline alkaloids (morphine).
 
• **Uses:** Alkaloids are used in various fields such as medicine (pain relief, anti-malaria), agriculture (pesticides), and research.
 
• **Solubility:** Free alkaloids are often insoluble in water but become water-soluble when converted to their salt forms through reactions with acids.
 
• **Common Sources:** Found in plants like coffee, tea, tobacco, and opium poppy, alkaloids are concentrated in specific parts such as leaves, roots, and seeds.

questions.question:
Which of the following statements is correct when an acid is dissolved in water?

a) The separation of H⁺ ions from HCl molecules cannot occur in the absence of water.

b) Hydrogen ions must always be shown as H⁺ (aq) or hydronium ion (H₃O⁺).
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both a and b**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The separation of **H+ ions** from **HCl molecules** indeed cannot occur in the absence of water. Water is necessary to facilitate the dissociation process.
 
• Hydrogen ions in an aqueous solution are always shown as **H+ (aq)** or **H3O+ (hydronium ion)**. This is because hydrogen ions cannot exist freely in water; they combine with water molecules to form hydronium ions.
 
• When an acid like **HCl** is dissolved in water, it dissociates into **H+ (aq)** and **Cl- (aq)**, demonstrating the necessity of water for this process.
 
• The correct representation of hydrogen ions in water as **H+ (aq)** or **H3O+** ensures a more accurate depiction of their behavior in solution.
 
• Both statements are correct and together they provide a comprehensive understanding of the behavior of acids in water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hydronium Ion (H3O+)**__

 __
 
• The hydronium ion is formed when a water molecule accepts a hydrogen ion (proton).
 
• It plays a key role in the chemistry of acids and bases in aqueous solutions.
 
• Hydronium ions are responsible for the acidic properties of solutions.
 
 
 
• **Dissociation in Water**__
 
 
• Dissociation is the process by which molecules split into smaller particles such as ions.
 
• This process is crucial in understanding the behavior of acids, bases, and salts in water.
 
• Water acts as a solvent and facilitates the dissociation of ionic compounds.

questions.question: Which ion is responsible for the acidic properties of acids?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**H⁺**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The presence of **H⁺ ions** in a solution is what makes an acid exhibit its **acidic properties**.
 
• When an acid is dissolved in water, it releases **hydrogen ions (H⁺)**, which are responsible for the **acidic nature** of the solution.
 
• The strength of an acid is determined by the concentration of **H⁺ ions** in the solution.
 
• **H⁺ ions** are also known as **protons**, and they can combine with water molecules to form **hydronium ions (H₃O⁺)**.
 
• The pH scale is used to measure the **acidity** or **alkalinity** of a solution, where a lower pH value indicates a higher concentration of **H⁺ ions** and thus a more **acidic solution**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **OH⁻**__

 __
 
• **Hydroxide ions (OH⁻)** are responsible for the **basic properties** of a solution.
 
• Bases release **OH⁻ ions** in solution, which can neutralize **H⁺ ions**.
 
 
 
• **Cl⁻**__
 __
 
• **Chloride ions (Cl⁻)** are typically found in **salts** and do not contribute to the **acidity** of a solution.
 
• For example, in hydrochloric acid (HCl), **H⁺** is responsible for acidity, while **Cl⁻** is the conjugate base.
 
 
 
• **Na⁺**__
 
 
• **Sodium ions (Na⁺)** are typically found in **salts** and do not contribute to the **acidity** of a solution.
 
• In solutions, **Na⁺ ions** are usually paired with anions and do not affect the pH significantly.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is least reactive with acids?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Copper**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Copper is one of the least reactive metals with acids, making it less likely to corrode or tarnish when exposed to acidic environments.
 
• In the reactivity series of metals, copper is placed below hydrogen, indicating its lower reactivity with acids.
 
• When copper reacts with acids, it does not produce hydrogen gas, unlike more reactive metals such as zinc or iron.
 
• Due to its low reactivity, copper is often used in plumbing, roofing, and electrical wiring where resistance to corrosion is essential.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Reactivity Series:**

 
 
• The reactivity series is a list of metals arranged in order of decreasing reactivity.
 
• Metals higher in the series react more vigorously with acids and other substances.
 
• Metals like potassium and sodium are highly reactive, while gold and platinum are the least reactive.
 
 
 
• **Hydrogen Production:**
 
 
• Reactive metals such as zinc and iron react with acids to produce hydrogen gas.
 
• Copper, being less reactive, does not produce hydrogen gas when it reacts with acids.
 
 
 
• **Corrosion Resistance:**
 
 
• Copper's resistance to corrosion is due to its low reactivity with environmental substances, including acids.
 
• This property makes copper suitable for use in various applications where long-term durability is required.
 
 
 
• **Uses of Copper:**
 
 
• Copper is extensively used in electrical wiring due to its excellent conductivity and resistance to corrosion.
 
• It is also used in plumbing, roofing, and industrial machinery.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs is an acid-base conjugate pair?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**NH₄⁺ and NH₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An **acid-base conjugate pair** consists of two chemical species that differ by a single proton (H⁺).
 
• **NH₄⁺** (ammonium ion) acts as an **acid** because it can donate a proton (H⁺).
 
• **NH₃** (ammonia) acts as a **base** because it can accept a proton.
 
• When **NH₄⁺** loses a proton, it becomes **NH₃**, and when **NH₃** gains a proton, it becomes **NH₄⁺**.
 
• This reversible exchange of a proton makes them an ideal **acid-base conjugate pair**.
 
• Such pairs are critical in understanding the behavior of acids and bases in chemical reactions, particularly in the context of the **Brønsted-Lowry theory.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **H⁺ and O²⁻**__

 __
 
• This is not an acid-base conjugate pair because **H⁺** is a proton, and **O²⁻** is an oxide ion. They do not differ by a single proton.
 
• However, oxide ions (**O²⁻**) can act as a strong base and react with protons (**H⁺**) to form water.
 
 
 
• **H₂O and H₂O₂**__
 __
 
• **H₂O (water)** and **H₂O₂ (hydrogen peroxide)** are not an acid-base conjugate pair because they differ by more than one atom or structure rather than by a single proton.
 
• **H₂O₂** is a strong oxidizing agent and has different chemical properties compared to **H₂O**.
 
 
 
• **HCl and Cl₂**__
 
 
• **HCl (hydrogen chloride)** is a strong acid, but **Cl₂ (chlorine gas)** is a diatomic molecule and does not act as a base in this context.
 
• These two species are not related by the gain or loss of a single proton.
 
• **HCl** is commonly used in various industrial and laboratory applications, including pH adjustment and chemical synthesis.
